# This world's context language (generated by the engine; do not hand-edit — regenerate after changing manifest.json → prompt)

## What the engine shows the model each turn (the pack)
In order: time · town / here / exits · place ids of this town · present characters and NPCs · player · personas · characters elsewhere · notes / rumors / lore · registered classes · engine messages · variables and their rules · recent narration.
Then the user block: tool results · character replies · relevant entries · the player now · (on refusal) the last proposal.

## What the model writes (output format)
## Output format
Follow this format exactly. Write nothing outside the blocks.
lines: the messages shown on screen, in order. A character's spoken line must be wrapped in quotation marks (starts with ", ends with "). A message without quotation marks is narration. Never put speech and narration in the same message. This feeds an ADV text panel: one sentence per line.
ops: this turn's state changes, one per line; if nothing changed write a single line: none. Allowed lines:
move <who> <to>          move: who = player or a present character / NPC's name; where = a place id of this town, or a new place name (grown on the spot if the map lacks it). Write the FINAL place of this turn, not the places passed; any place in town is reachable in one turn
[ask <who>]              request: a present character must answer before you can go on; at most two per turn
player.hp -3          variable: name + number; a leading + / − adds, no sign sets
flag <key>               story flag
new_location <name> <parent> <links> new place (writer): new_location <name> plus where it sits in the map's tree — near=<A>[,<B>] same layer, beside them; between=<A>,<B> on the road between; in=<A> inside A (one layer down, entered only through A); over=<A>,<B> wrapping places of one layer (one layer up, e.g. a district). Unsure: leave it out — it hangs beside the player and is placed from the prose after the turn
link <a> <b>             a new path: link <place A> <place B> (two places of one town not yet connected, e.g. a shortcut found)
unlink <a> <b>           a path is cut: unlink <place A> <place B> (bridge down, road sealed; refused if it would cut a part of town off)
new_town <name> <from> <days> <summary> <tags> new town (writer): when the player heads for a town the world map does not have yet, the world grows it — new_town <name> from=<town the road starts at> days=<days on the road> summary=<one line> tags=<road tags, comma-separated>; then travel there as usual
new_npc <name> <at> <role> 新路人(writer)
new <class> <name>       a new instance of a registered class (only when the pack lists registrable classes)
patch <who> <props>      开放 schema:给任何一个人 / 物 / 地方写属性,写成 patch <名字> 属性=值 …;新属性直接加,写进它自己的记录(声明过的属性只限可变的;名字、id、位置不能改——让谁去哪儿用 move)
remove <who>             开放 schema:一个实例离开世界(用光了、结束了),写成 remove <名字>
write <path>             file: create or replace a .json / .md / .txt in the world folder — [~write path]content[/write] (JSON must parse; paths relative to the world folder)
edit <path>              file: set keys in a JSON file — edit <path> key=value … (dots nest; new keys are added)
rm <path>                file: delete a file — rm <path> (only what was made in play or lives in the open-schema folder)
mkdir <path>             folder: create — mkdir <path>
rmdir <path>             folder: delete one made in play (with its files) — rmdir <path>
define <kind> <name>     open schema: when the world needs a kind of thing it does not have yet, define it on the spot — define class <name> <title> prop=type … (int/str/bool/list, choices a|b|c) mutable=props,… (effect=yes: a state that runs each turn); define var <name> <type> <initial> min= max=. Usable at once with new / patch / remove / the variable
[roll <dice>]            request: dice as 1d6 / 2d10 / 2d6+1; never invent the number
[dice <dice> <vs>]       check: [dice 1d20+2 vs 12]what is tested and why[/dice]; the engine returns the number and pass/fail
[~map]                   map: [~map] — the engine draws the current place from real state (town / dungeon / road) straight to the player; not awaited, keep writing; never draw maps yourself
[~sheet]                 sheet: [~sheet] — the engine shows the player's stats / pack / purse as a panel; not awaited; never read numbers into the prose
[referee <question>]     ask the rules referee: [referee what the player attempts]; it rules on rules + sheet, you write by the ruling
[combat …]…[/combat]     switch to the combat layer: [combat bandit×5 boss×1]why it starts[/combat]; name×count in the tag is the roster (engine builds them), the body the hand-off; lines stop there, the combat referee continues
end_combat <outcome>     combat layer only: end_combat outcome=won|fled|lost
none
options: 2–4 things the player might say or do next. Short (under 12 words), pointing in different directions (friendly / confrontational / change the subject …). One option per line.
An action may also be written inline in lines, equivalent to an ops line: [~move player inn]You push the inn door open., or [~flag paid]. A request in square brackets stops the lines at that line; the engine answers and you continue. The engine speaks back to you in angle brackets: <event>/<end> are things that happened, <say> a character's line, <roll 1d6>4</roll> a request's answer, <refused> why something was refused.

EXAMPLE OUTPUT:
<lines>
You push open the door of the River Lantern Inn; the hearth's warmth touches your face.
"One room. Two of us."
Mira looks up from the counter and takes the two of you in.
"Eight coins a night, paid up front."
Elena says nothing and shakes the fog from her cloak.
</lines>
<ops>
move player inn
move Elena inn
player.gold -8
</ops>
<options>
"Pay for one night"
Ask Mira about Rowan
"Too expensive"
Turn around and leave
</options>

## The context language: the bracket says whether the turn waits
- `[tag args]` a sync request: lines stop at that line; the engine answers and the model continues (`[dice 1d20+2 vs 12]why[/dice]`, `[referee what the player attempts]`, `[ask Elena]`, `[combat bandit×3]hand-off[/combat]`)
- `[~tag args]` an async action: not awaited, the engine does it and the model keeps writing (`[~move player inn]`, `[~flag paid]`, `[~player.gold -3]`, `[~map]`); same as one ops line
- The engine's registry decides which ops wait (each op declares `wait`); a wrong bracket is executed by the registry and logged in the trace
- The old form `<move player inn>` is still read, as `[~move player inn]`
The engine speaks back in angle brackets: `<event id>what happened</event>` · `<end id>epilogue hint</end>` · `<say name attitude=…>line</say>` · `<roll 1d6>4</roll>` · `<refused op field>why; allowed: …</refused>`.

## Entries (manifest.json → "prompt" → "entries"; play-time changes in game/meta/prompt.json)
- `"when": "always"` goes into the system prompt; `"post"` goes last; conditional ones (`{"keyword": …}` · `{"at": …}` · `{"var": …, ">=": n}` · `{"flag": …}`) are injected next to the player's line when they hold.
- `rules` / `voice` / `blocks` / `ops_docs` live here too. Three layers: the template's pack.json < manifest.json < game/meta/prompt.json.
